R5B-bear-backcountry-0001.name: By Nusash Creek
R5B-bear-backcountry-0001.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R5B-bear-backcountry-0001.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2014 (12 years old), 130 m SE: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2019 (fire VA0920), 50 m E: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SW facing slope, 19 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Nusash Creek 40 m SW: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Stuie, about 68 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 52.39145, -126.83488, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 29 km NW, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 3,846 m, about 968 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 780 m NW of the spot at 2 m (52.61328, -127.08388). Water: Nusash Creek 110 m S (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 5-9, Region 5. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-09-10, closures 2026-10-16.

evidence.t: Mule deer winter range u-5-005 unit 14-219 (official), right here. Counts from October.
Habitat zone Coastal Western Hemlock (CWHws2): coast forest, where black tailed deer are among the most common large mammals (95%) and use logged ground often (80%) (lesson: Wet forests).
SE facing slope, 15 degrees: sun melts snow first.
Private fields 1.6 km NE: deer feed on field edges (fields are private).
